Casio Announces G-Shock Mudman GDG-B100; Features MIP LCD, Light Fitness Tracking

No Tough Solar though, so it’s running on a CR2032 battery.

by Ian Chee
October 5, 2026

Image: Casio

222
SHARES
Share on WhatsappShare on TelegramThreads
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:05
Instaread

Casio has launched its Mudman GDG-B100 series of G-Shock watches, which consists of three colour options. As you’d expect from a series that’s aimed at hikers, and outdoors people in general, you get a pretty rugged watch case that measures in at 63.6 × 49.6 × 16.2 mm, and weighing 66g. Notebookcheck reports that case construction consists of carbon fibre-reinforced resin, as well as what is called Carbon Core Guard structure.

Adding to the rugged nature is mud resistance plus dust sealing, as well as a water resistance of up to 200m to go with that vaguely off-road vehicle look. Oddly enough, it doesn’t feature Casio’s Tough Solar charging tech, nor does it use rechargeable batteries. Instead, the Mudman GDG-B100 uses pretty conventional CR2032 batteries, with the watch rated to get two years of use out of these.

×

The report also notes that this is the first Mudman model to sport what Casio calls the Memory-in-Pixel (MIP) display. If you’re unfamiliar, it’s an LCD display that can stay readable even in bright sunlight while keeping power consumption low. Making it a little unique is its LED backlight, which is red instead of the usual white or blue, to let you maintain your adjusted night vision better.

As you may expect from a pretty modern watch, it comes with things like Smartphone Link for some light smartwatch-esque features. Complementing this are a small suite of fitness tracking features with the help of the built-in accelerometer. You can log up to 100 runs with as many as 140 laps each, with details on your distance, speed and pace being tracked. Overall, it’s pretty much like a replaceable battery version of the G-Squad GBD-H2000.

×

That being said, the Casio G-Shock Mudman GDG-B100 series – which consists of the black B100-1, the green 1A3 and the sand 1A5 – is not currently listed on Casio Malaysia’s website. In Japan though, all three are priced at JPY 38,500 (~RM996). For now, there’s no word on if these will be available locally.

(Source: Casio [1], [2], [3] via Notebookcheck)

Rapid KL To Conduct Pilot Project For Fixed-Route Feeder Vans Starting 24 October

This will last for three months.

by Ian Chee
October 21, 2026

Image: Prasarana

Share on WhatsappShare on TelegramThreads

Rapid KL has announced that it will be conducting pilot testing for fixed-route feeder buses for three months. This is set to start at the end of the week, or more specifically, on 24 October. The public transport network said that this is aimed at strengthening public transport connectivity, and that the initiative supports the government’s aspiration to increase public transport ridership through a more integrated, accessible, and sustainable mobility system.

For the duration of the pilot, passengers will be charged a fare of RM1 per trip, payment for which can be made using debit and credit cards, as well as Touch ‘n Go cards. Holders of MyRapid Concession Cards can get a 50% discount on the fare, while Rapid Mesra pass holders don’t get charged at all. These vans will have a frequency of between 15 and 20 minutes, and passengers can board these vans at designated stations and stops without needing to book them via the Rapid On-Demand app.

That being said, two Rapid KL On Demand service zones will be suspended for the duration of the pilot’s first phase. The first of these is the T400B zone, which connects Bandar Tun Razak to Taman Midah, linking the Bandar Tun Razak station on the Sri Petaling Line and the Taman Midah station on the Kajang Line. Then there’s the T512B service zone, which runs from Precinct 11 to Putrajaya Sentral, connecting the Putrajaya Sentral station to both the Putrajaya Line and the KLIA Transit (ERL) service.

Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki, CEO of Rapid Bus, said that this is part of Rapid KL’s ongoing efforts to increase public transport ridership. “Through this pilot project, Rapid KL will evaluate an operational model based on fixed routes and schedules to enhance first- and last-mile connectivity, thereby improving community access to nearby rail stations”, he said. “Findings gathered throughout the implementation period will serve as a reference for considering future service improvements”.

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
  • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
